# Discussion

**What the surprise is.** The interesting finding is not that a 270M
model fails the behavioral \(a\)/\(an\) demo---@hanna2026latent already
place reliable success at larger scales. The surprise is the
**juxtaposition** inside editable mechanisms: the same sparse features
that cleanly switch legal packages under free generation still fail as
independent content dials once \(b\) is held fixed, even after within-class
targets, per-noun Latent-Planning-style selection, and a dense residual
steer. Packaging and \(b\to c\) are easy to move; modular
\(C\to c\) is not.

**Methodological implication.** Article-only attribution and free
generation overstate modular planning whenever noun changes can be
explained by \(b\to c\). Edge tests that paste native \(b\)
**while keeping content edits active** should be standard before claiming
separable forward/backward planning from feature interventions.

**Relation to Latent Planning.** We do not claim their large-model
results are wrong, nor that latent planning is impossible. We claim that
on this small model, dual-effect / content-attributed interventions are
better explained as H2 packagers than as H1 modular planners, and that
the independent-content edge required by a strong modular reading is
missing from the handles we could edit.
